remarks_1999: Double entries Downtown Gallery Archive. Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "Given to Arthur Dove in exchange for one of his pictures. O'Keeffe thinks about 1919." Dove's descendants believe Dove purchased the painting. See *Dear Stieglitz, Dear Dove* (1988), p. 95. Whitney Archive dates c. 1919. Abiquiú Notebooks dates 1919. Downtown Gallery Archive dates 1919 and 1928/1930. Pictured in 1923 New York (Anderson) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 13. Mrs. Weiner, referred to in stretcher inscription 1, was O'Keeffe's friend, Alma Morganthau (Mrs. Maurice Wertheim [1909–29], Mrs. Paul Weiner [1935]), of Cos Cob, Connecticut (stretcher inscription written after work in possession of Dove). Works related to O'Keeffe's visits to Cos Cob in the 1920s included cat. nos. 370–72, 547, 612, 613, 627, 1943–46. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A narrow, light gray form arches and expands from the bottom to the top of the composition, creating a sense of movement. Two darker, bluish-gray shapes curve upward on either side of the light gray shape. The background of the composition is rendered in geometric black and brown forms.
